What Did “Palestinian” Mean Before 1948? A short historical look at how the words “Palestine” and “Palestinian” were used during the British Mandate. At the time, Palestinian citizenship could apply to both Arab and Jewish residents, while institutions such as the Palestine Orchestra and Anglo-Palestine Bank were connected to the developing Jewish community and Zionist movement.  The point of the video is simple: historical terms should be understood in their historical context, rather than automatically given their modern political meaning. Watch the examples and make up your own mind. #History #MiddleEastHistory #PalestineHistory #IsraelHistory #BritishMandate

During the war in Gaza, there were moments when people gathered in the west of Gaza City, looking up at the sky, waiting for aid to fall from airplanes. People ran through the streets and open areas, hoping to catch a bag of flour, rice, or a small box of food. For many families, it was not simply aid—it was a desperate attempt to survive another day. Children watched from a distance, while exhausted parents searched through the crowds for anything they could bring back to their families. No one should have to wait for food to fall from the sky just to survive. Behind every crowd was a family, a story, and a life changed by war. 💔 #HumanityForGaza  #Gaza #GazaWar #HumanitarianCrisis #Palestine #GazaChildren #Humanity #Aid #FoodCrisis #HelpGaza
